seo_title: SAP S/4HANA MRP Live (MD01N) vs Classic MRP (MD01)
h1: SAP S/4HANA MRP Live (MD01N) vs Classic MRP (MD01): Architecture, Differences and Migration
meta_description: SAP S/4HANA MRP Live vs classic MRP explained: MD01N vs MD01, how each runs, what changes for you, and how to move plants over. Read the full guide.
excerpt: How SAP S/4HANA MRP Live (MD01N) differs from classic MRP (MD01): where the logic runs, what you configure, what to test, and how to cut plants over safely.
intro_html:
Most S/4HANA conversion projects hit the same MRP question in the first workshop: "Our nightly MRP run takes six hours in ECC. Will it be faster, and will our planners see the same results?" The honest answer needs you to know what actually differs between SAP S/4HANA MRP Live and classic MRP, and what does not.

This guide explains how MRP Live (MD01N) executes compared with classic MRP (MD01), which inputs and outputs stay the same, where the behaviour or the screens change, and how to test and cut over plant by plant. It is written for MM/PP consultants who must explain this to a client, and for freshers who will be asked about it in interviews.

sections.heading: What MRP Live actually changes (and what it does not)
sections.html:
MRP's job is unchanged: look at stock, receipts and requirements, calculate shortages, and create planned orders, purchase requisitions or schedule lines. The planning logic you know (MRP types, lot-sizing, safety stock, planned delivery time, BOM explosion, procurement proposals) is the same business logic.

What changes is where the calculation runs. In classic MRP, the ABAP application server reads planning data from the database material by material, calculates in application-server memory, and writes the results back. In MRP Live, the calculation is pushed down into the SAP HANA database using ABAP-managed database procedures, so far less data travels between the database and the application server. This is the same code-pushdown idea described in ABAP on HANA code pushdown.

AspectClassic MRPMRP Live
Total planning transactionMD01MD01N
Where the calculation runsABAP application serverSAP HANA database (database procedures)
Database platformAny supported database (ECC)HANA only
Planning filePlanning file entries in DBVMSame concept; net change logic is retained
ResultsPlanned orders (PLAF), purchase requisitions (EBAN), schedule lines, MRP listsSame documents
AnalysisMD04, MD05, MD06, MD07Same transactions
ECC vs S/4HANA: MRP Live is only available on S/4HANA (it was introduced with the first S/4HANA releases and later made the default recommendation). In ECC you only have classic MRP, even if your ECC database is HANA (Suite on HANA).

Because master data, document types and downstream steps are unchanged, a planner still sees the same stock/requirements list. The main differences you will notice are runtime, parallelisation behaviour and a few functional or enhancement-related restrictions, covered below.

sections.heading: How MRP Live executes on the HANA database
sections.html:
Think of classic MRP as a long conveyor belt: for each material, fetch rows, bring them to the application server, calculate, write back. With millions of requirement and receipt rows, the cost is mostly data transfer and row-by-row processing.

MRP Live reverses this. The planning run selects the materials in scope, and the heavy parts (reading stock and requirements, netting, lot-sizing, low-level BOM handling) execute inside HANA, close to the data, using set-based processing and parallelism that the database manages. Only the final results are returned to be stored as planned orders or requisitions.

Practical consequences

  • Run time: the gain is largest for big plants with many materials, deep multi-level BOMs and many open requirements. Small plants with few materials may see little change.
  • Memory: work moves from the application server to HANA, so watch HANA memory and CPU during the run, not only application work processes. See S/4HANA system architecture for BASIS beginners for the layers involved.
  • Planning frequency: faster runs let some businesses plan more often than once a night, which is the real business value, not just a shorter job log.
Tip: Never promise the client a specific speed-up factor. Measure it on a copy of their production data. Gains depend on data volume, BOM depth, custom code and hardware.

sections.heading: MD01N vs MD01: screen and parameter comparison
sections.html:
Both transactions let you plan a plant (total planning), but the selection screen and options differ. Open both in your sandbox side by side and compare.

ItemMD01 (classic)MD01N (MRP Live)
Plant / planning scopePlant, optional planning scopePlant or MRP area, optional planning scope
Processing keyNETCH net change, NETPL net change in planning horizon, NEUPL regenerative planningSame three planning types
Create purchase requisitionsOption 1/2/3 (opening period logic)Same options
MRP list creationOption to create MRP listsOption available
Planning mode / schedulingAdapt, re-explode, delete and recreateSame planning modes
Parallel processingApplication-server parallel processing using RFC server groupsParallelisation by the database; no application-server RFC group tuning
Online result displayMore online display optionsFewer; analyse results in MD04 / MD07 afterwards

Single-item planning (MD02 multi-level, MD03 single-level) and the planning-file maintenance transactions remain part of the toolset, and planners keep using MD04, MD05 and MD06 for analysis. Always check the exact options in your own release, because SAP has widened MRP Live coverage release by release.

Interview angle: "What is the difference between MD01 and MD01N?" A good answer: same business logic and results, but MD01N executes the calculation in HANA instead of the application server, so it is faster on large volumes and uses database parallelism rather than RFC-group parallel processing.

sections.heading: Functional restrictions and custom code to review
sections.html:
The main risk in an MRP Live move is not the standard planning logic. It is anything that depended on code running in the application server for each material.

1. Custom enhancements

Classic MRP lets custom code (BAdIs, user exits, modifications) intervene during the run. Logic that is executed in the database cannot call arbitrary ABAP per material, so enhancements that change planning results must be reviewed. Inventory every enhancement on MRP objects, and check SAP's documentation for your release to see which hooks are still supported and which are replaced by alternative extension points.

2. Release-specific functional coverage

In early S/4HANA releases MRP Live did not cover every classic feature. Coverage has improved since, but you must not assume it. Use these sources for your exact release:

  • The Simplification Item Catalog and the Simplification List for your target release.
  • The release's What's New and application help for MRP.
  • The SAP Readiness Check for S/4HANA conversions, which flags relevant simplification items from your own system.

Also read what changed in the S/4HANA 2025 release for MM and EWM consultants for recent changes.

3. Master-data hygiene

Dirty data hurts both modes, but the cleanup is easier before you switch. Check the MRP views of the material master (see material master views, field by field): MRP type (DISMM), MRP controller (DISPO), lot size (DISLS), planned delivery time (PLIFZ), procurement type and special procurement key.

Warning: Do not move a plant to MD01N in production because a demo ran well. Compare classic versus MRP Live results on the same data first. A different planned order for the same material is a finding to investigate, not noise.

sections.heading: Migration approach: moving plants to MRP Live
sections.html:
A plant-by-plant approach lowers risk because MRP is planned per plant. Use the steps below as a project template.

  1. Assess: run the readiness/simplification check for your release and list MRP-related items. Inventory custom code on MRP objects.
  2. Clean master data: fix materials with missing MRP controller, wrong lot size or MRP type, and obsolete planning file entries.
  3. Copy and baseline: in a test system with production-like data, run classic MD01 with NEUPL (regenerative) for the plant and export results (planned orders, requisitions) as a baseline.
  4. Reset and re-run: restore the same data and run MD01N with the same parameters.
  5. Compare: check quantities, dates, order types and exception messages per material. Use MD04 for samples and a custom report or extract for the full list.
  6. Time it: record run time and HANA resource usage, including the background job window.
  7. Cut over: change the background job variant (SM36/SM37) or the scheduling app from MD01 to MD01N for the first plant, and monitor for a few cycles before the next plant.

A worked example: Plant 1000 has 45,000 MRP-relevant materials. After the regenerative baseline run, classic MRP creates 3,210 planned orders and 1,480 purchase requisitions. The MRP Live run produces the same totals, but 14 materials differ by a few days in the planned start date. Investigation shows they use a custom scheduling enhancement. That is exactly the kind of finding the comparison is designed to surface, and you fix it before go-live.

Tip: Keep a small "golden set" of 30 to 50 materials covering make-to-stock, purchased, phantom, subcontracting and long-lead items. The business can sign off on the golden set faster than on 45,000 results. Subcontracting planning is covered in the subcontracting process guide.

sections.heading: Scheduling, monitoring and what planners see afterwards
sections.html:
Operational use is where the change gets noticed day to day.

  • Background scheduling: total planning is normally a nightly background job (SM36). Check job logs in SM37 and the MRP log after each run.
  • Fiori apps: S/4HANA offers MRP apps such as Monitor Material Coverage and an app for scheduling MRP runs. App availability and names vary by release, so confirm them in the Fiori apps reference library for your version.
  • Analysis transactions: MD04 (stock/requirements list), MD05 (MRP list), MD06 (MRP list collective display) and MD07 (stock/requirements list collective display) are unchanged for planners.
  • Downstream: planned orders convert to production orders (CO40/CO41) and requisitions to POs, manually or by automation. See automatic PO creation with ME59N and the purchase order cycle guide.
Background: Net change planning relies on planning file entries that are created when stock or requirements change. Switching between MD01 and MD01N does not require a new data model, but the first run after a cutover is often done as regenerative planning (NEUPL) so everyone starts from a clean, known state.

Joule and other AI assistants are beginning to read MRP exception messages for planners. See the Joule logistics and procurement blueprint if the client asks about it, but the underlying MRP results still come from the same run.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and common mistakes
sections.html:
SymptomLikely causeFix
Materials not planned at allMRP type ND, missing MRP controller, or material not in the planning scopeCheck MM03 MRP 1 view and the planning scope; run MD03 for one material to see the result
Result differs from classic MRPCustom enhancement or scheduling logic not applied in the database runReview enhancements; compare using the golden set
Run is slow despite MRP LiveLarge result volume, locked materials, undersized HANA resources, or heavy custom codeCheck job log, HANA load (DBACOCKPIT or HANA Cockpit), and run during a quiet period
Material skipped because it is lockedAnother user or job is changing or planning the same materialCheck SM12 locks and overlapping jobs; reschedule so jobs do not overlap
No new proposals after net change runNo planning file entry because nothing relevant changedConfirm the change, or run regenerative planning (NEUPL) for that scope
Too many purchase requisitionsWrong requisition creation option or an unrealistic planned delivery timeCheck parameters and PLIFZ; compare to your classic baseline
Common mistakes: (1) judging MRP Live only by run time, not result accuracy; (2) skipping the custom-code inventory; (3) running regenerative planning in production during working hours; (4) changing the job variant without telling planners, so they cannot explain different run times or timestamps.

sections.heading: Interview questions on this topic
sections.html:
1. Why is MRP Live faster? The calculation runs inside HANA close to the data, so there is less data transfer and the database parallelises the work.
  2. Does MRP Live change the MRP logic? No. Planning types, lot sizes, MRP types and procurement proposals remain the same business logic. The execution layer changes.
  3. Can you use MD01 in S/4HANA? Check your release. The transaction may still exist, but MD01N is the recommended choice for total planning in S/4HANA.
  4. What would you check before moving a plant to MRP Live? Custom enhancements, release restrictions in the simplification list, master-data quality, a classic-vs-live result comparison and run-time measurement.
  5. Where do you analyse MRP results? MD04 for one material, MD07 for collective stock/requirements, MD06 for MRP lists, plus Fiori apps.
How to answer: Start with the business outcome (faster, more frequent planning), then the technical reason (database pushdown), then the project risk (enhancements and validation). Interviewers also see this in scenario-based MM interviews. Practising the comparison on an S/4HANA sandbox makes your answer much more convincing.

For where MRP fits in the wider process chain, read end-to-end SAP logistics integration.

key_takeaways: MRP Live (MD01N) keeps the same planning logic as classic MRP (MD01) but runs the calculation inside the SAP HANA database instead of the ABAP application server.
The speed benefit depends on data volume, BOM depth, custom code and hardware, so measure it on production-like data rather than promising a factor.
Custom enhancements on MRP and release-specific functional coverage are the main risks; check the simplification list for your exact release.
Migrate plant by plant: baseline with classic regenerative planning, re-run in MD01N, compare results using a golden set of materials, then cut over the job.
Analysis stays familiar: MD04, MD05, MD06 and MD07 still show MRP results for planners.

faqs.question: What is MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA?
faqs.answer: MRP Live is the S/4HANA version of total MRP, run with transaction MD01N. It performs the planning calculation in the SAP HANA database rather than in the ABAP application server, which reduces data transfer and improves run time on large data volumes.

faqs.question: Is MRP Live always faster than classic MRP?
faqs.answer: It is usually faster for large plants with many materials and open requirements, but the gain varies. Small plants, heavy custom code or limited HANA resources can reduce the benefit, so measure on a copy of real data.

faqs.question: Do planning results change when I move from MD01 to MD01N?
faqs.answer: They should not, because the business logic is the same. Differences usually come from custom enhancements, data issues or release-specific restrictions, which is why you compare a classic baseline with an MRP Live run before cutover.

faqs.question: Can I run MRP Live on ECC?
faqs.answer: No. MRP Live is an S/4HANA capability. ECC, even when running on a HANA database, uses classic MRP via MD01.

faqs.question: Which transactions do planners use to review MRP Live results?
faqs.answer: The usual ones: MD04 for the stock/requirements list of one material, MD05 for the MRP list, MD06 for the collective MRP list and MD07 for the collective stock/requirements list. Fiori apps for material coverage are also available.

faqs.question: Do I need to change master data to use MRP Live?
faqs.answer: There is no new master-data model, but you should clean existing data such as MRP controller, MRP type, lot size and planned delivery time. Doing so before the move makes the result comparison much easier.

faqs.question: How should I cut over production plants to MD01N?
faqs.answer: Go one plant at a time. Baseline with classic regenerative planning in test, run MD01N on the same data, compare results and timing, then update the background job and monitor several cycles before moving the next plant.
